As the $\mathrm{IrO}_{2}$ content increases,the electrocatalytic activity for OER increased rapidly (Fig. 4a), and reaches its optimization when the Ir content is 16 wt%. However, a further increase in the Ir content of the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ results in a slight deterioration of the electrocatalytic activity. The required overpotential to generate a current density of $10\mathrm{m A}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ (normalized over the electrode geometric area) for 16 wt%$\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ is 288 mV, lower than that of unsupported $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}\left(307\mathrm{m V}\right)$ The Tafel slope of 16 wt%$\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 2is 42.6 mV dec-1 (Supplementary Fig. 8), close to that of unsupported $\mathbf{I r O}_{2}$ (45.1mV dec-1),indicating that the the $\mathsf{T a B}_{2}$ _support has no change to OER pathway of $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$

Electrochemical double layer capacitance (DLC) measurements were carried out to obtain the electrochemically active surface area $\left(\mathrm{E C S A}\right)\mathrm{o f}\mathrm{I r O}_{2}@\mathrm{T a B}_{2}$ by estimating the accumulated charge amount at the electrode surface. Generally, the ECSA values become larger with increasing Ir content in $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 2 (Fig. 4b, left and Supplementary Table 6). In order to compare the intrinsic activities of different catalysts, we normalized the measured currents by the ECSAs (Fig. 4b,right). The 16 wt%$\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ presents the highest current density $(j_{ECSA})$ at 1.53V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) among these $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ ,samples, which is 5.2 times larger than that of $\mathbf{I r O}_{2},$ We further compared the iridium mass activities of $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ and $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ by normalizing the measured currents over the mass of iridium $(j_{\mathrm{i r}})$ . Although 16%$\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ has 70 wt% less iridium relative to $\mathbf{I r O}_{2}$ ,it displays a high iridium mass activity of $345\mathrm{A g^{-1}}$ at $1.53\mathrm{V}$ versus RHE

We further compare the performance of PEMWEs using $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ and commercial $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ as anode electrocatalysts (Fig. 5c),under the similar Ir loading in CCM. While $\mathsf{I r O}_{2}$ employing as anode layer, the PEMWE delivers a significantly lower current density of $1.9\mathrm{A}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ relative to $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ :catalyst $(3.06\mathrm{A}\mathrm{c m}^{-2})$ at 2.0Vcell potential. To evaluate catalyst stability, the $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ and IrO₂@TaB2 anode cells were tested at a constant current density of 1$1\mathrm{A}\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ The PEMWE using $\mathrm{I r O}_{2}$ anode undergoes a severe deactivation under the low Ir loading of $0.2\mathrm{m g}\mathrm{c m}^{-2}$ , and the $\mathrm{I r O_{2}}$ anode cell exhibits reasonable stability when the Ir loading increases to 2mg $\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ (Fig. 5e and Supplementary Fig.21-24).By comparison, the PEMWE using $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ 1anode provides a steady operation for more than 120 h under a low Ir loading of 0.15 mgcm2(Fig.5e),confirming excellentcatalytic stability. We can speculate that the $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$  with larger material volume can forms a thicker catalyst layer relative to bare $\mathrm{I r O}_{2},$ ,so that the former possesses sufficient layer conductivity and stability at such a low Ir loading. The great activity and stability demonstrate the great potential of $\mathrm{IrO_{2}@TaB_{2}}$ as a practical anode of real PEMwE for commercial application.
